decision: Keep as a statically validated candidate; do not claim faster laps, completion improvement, SOTA or submission readiness without an authorized controlled environment evaluation.
implementation: Infer entry, apex and confirmed exit phases only from generic visible road geometry at rows30,34,42 and54; no track, seed, elapsed-time or coordinate condition is used.
Use bounded outside/inside/outside lateral references0.18/-0.10/0.18 with a0.035 correction cap and at least7.0 pixels of predicted geometric edge clearance.
Require consecutive confirmation for exit and clear transitions, reset ambiguous state, and preserve left/right mirror symmetry.

Copy gas and brake from a reset-synchronized frozen completion controller on every frame. During a current obstacle or its miss latch, copy that controller's complete action and synchronize steering state so the racing line cannot weaken obstacle avoidance.

evidence.finding: The latest videos do not support a universal in-in-in diagnosis: sampled track1 is approximately center-in-out, one track2 corner is out-out-out, and another is in-ish-in-ish-out. The factor is therefore a generic bounded geometry hypothesis, not a correction asserted from all observed turns.
evidence.interpretation: Minimum-curvature racing-line results motivate enlarging turn radius, but do not establish that a local camera-space out-in-out heuristic is globally minimum-time without track bounds and vehicle dynamics.
